questions.question: Explain why it is absolutely necessary to convert the Horizontal Equivalent into meters before calculating the final gradient ratio.
questions.expected_answer: To establish a valid mathematical ratio, both the numerator (Vertical Interval) and the denominator (Horizontal Equivalent) must share the identical unit of measurement. Dividing meters by kilometers produces an invalid ratio.

questions.question: If you are given a final gradient of 1:12, what does the '12' represent in the real world?
questions.expected_answer: The '12' represents the horizontal distance traveled for every 1 unit of vertical rise or fall. Specifically, it means you must walk 12 meters horizontally to experience a 1 meter change in elevation.
